overview: Despatch reports 1931 Seiyūkai-era personnel changes in Taiwan's colonial government: Ohta's resignation, Minami's appointment, Hiratsuka replacing Kinoshita, and military leadership changes, plus comments on Taiwan's strategic/commercial value, South China/South Seas ties, and military censorship of civilian administration.

people.name: Tsuyoshi Inukai
people.role: Prime Minister of Japan and head of the Seiyūkai cabinet

people.name: Hiroshi Minami
people.role: Member of the House of Peers and newly appointed Governor-General of Taiwan

people.name: Kinmochi Saionji
people.role: Prince, elder statesman, and former employer and political associate of Hiroshi Minami

people.name: Kinoshita
people.role: Former Director-General of the Taiwan Government-General

people.name: Jinzaburō Masaki
people.role: Former commander of the Japanese forces in Taiwan and newly appointed assistant chief of the Army General Staff

people.name: Nobuyuki Abe
people.role: Commander-in-chief of the Japanese forces in Taiwan; formerly commander of the Osaka division

subfiles.title: Despatch from Ketcham on personnel changes in the Taiwan Government-General
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports changes in the senior civil and military leadership of colonial Taiwan following the formation of the Seiyūkai cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Ketcham reports Ohta's resignation, Minami's appointment (noting his Saionji ties), Hiratsuka replacing Kinoshita and stressing Taiwan's South China/Philippine/Malaysia commercial role, General Masaki's promotion and replacement by Abe, and military censorship of the civilian administration.

interest: Shows metropolitan party politics reshaping colonial Taiwan's leadership, with Taiwan framed as a commercial expansion base.
